title: The Second CACHE Challenge - Targeting the RNA-Binding Pocket of the SARS-CoV2 Nonstructural Protein 13 via a consensus-scoring method and FITTED templated docking.
authors: Anita K. Nivedha; Mihai Burai-Patrascu; Ophélie Rostaing; Prakash Chukka; Bimaldeep Singh; Matej Janezic; Antoine Moitessier; Nicolas Moitessier; Joshua Pottel
one_liner_zh: 该文针对SARS-CoV2 NSP13 RNA结合口袋进行虚拟筛选，虽涉及蛋白-RNA互作与AI/对接方法，但对象非TF-DNA体系，且聚焦药物筛选而非结合机制建模，方法可迁移但匹配度中等。
abstract: Disrupting the Nonstructural Protein 13 (NSP13) in SARS-CoV2 could provide a great avenue for the treatment of COVID-19 and help reduce its enormous health burden. As part of the second CACHE challenge, we targeted each of two sub-pockets of the NSP13 RNA-binding site via a multi-pronged virtual screening (VS) campaign, using the latest functionality in FITTED, our docking program, part of the FORECASTER drug discovery suite. After extensive structure preparation and docking (rigid, flexible), we evaluated predicted poses from the VS using four approaches: docking score, machine learning (graph neural network), quantum-mechanics, and visualization, with the final selection being based on the consensus of all four approaches. Additionally, we implemented templated docking within FITTED to take advantage of fragments co-crystallized with NSP13, which supplemented our consensus selection. We now await the experimental testing of our predictions by the Structural Genomics Consortium, and once available, we will update this manuscript accordingly. In sharing our approach and findings, we hope to continue contributing to open science, and engaging in the ongoing effort of the scientific community towards ending COVID-19.
abstract_zh: 破坏SARS-CoV2中的非结构蛋白13（NSP13）可能为治疗COVID-19提供重要途径，并有助于减轻其巨大的健康负担。作为第二次CACHE挑战的一部分，我们通过多管齐下的虚拟筛选（VS）活动，针对NSP13 RNA结合位点的两个子口袋，利用我们对接程序FITTED中的最新功能，该程序是FORECASTER药物发现套件的一部分。在广泛的结构准备和对接（刚性、柔性）之后，我们使用四种方法评估了虚拟筛选中的预测姿态：对接评分、机器学习（图神经网络）、量子力学和可视化，最终选择基于所有四种方法的共识。此外，我们在FITTED中实施了模板化对接，以利用与NSP13共结晶的片段，这补充了我们的共识选择。我们现在等待结构基因组学联盟对我们预测的实验测试，一旦结果可用，我们将相应更新此手稿。通过分享我们的方法和发现，我们希望继续为开放科学做出贡献，并参与科学界为终结COVID-19而持续进行的努力。
